title: Development of a Monitoring Method for Mangrove Forests Using Multitemporal DSMs
content:
ABSTRACT

Monitoring forest changes over large areas with high accuracy is achievable using multitemporal digital surface models (DSMs). One of the key advantages of DSMs created from uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) platforms (UAV-DSM) is their high temporal and spatial resolution. However, the full potential of multitemporal UAV-DSM for forest monitoring has not been fully explored. This study aimed to demonstrate its effectiveness in monitoring mangrove forests. I analyzed time-series changes using UAV-DSM datasets from 13 periods (2015–2024) to assess the decline and growth of mangrove forests (2.8 ha) at the mouth of the Okukubi River on Okinawa Island, Japan. The average of the 13 UAV-DSMs was calculated using hexagonal tessellation, and time-series clustering was applied to analyze the data. This analysis enabled us to distinguish areas of growth from areas of decline. One key advantage of this approach is that it can generate clusters that reflect both the rate of change (increase or decrease) and the specific periods in which those changes occurred. Strong winds from typhoons and increased river flow due to rainfall have been suggested as causes for the disappearance of mangroves along riverbanks.
